chapters.title: The beginning of knowledge and wisdom’s invitation

parts.text: The proverbs are introduced as instruction in wisdom, justice, judgment, and understanding for both inexperienced and wise readers. Knowledge begins with fearing the LORD, while fools despise correction. A son is urged to heed his parents and refuse companions who promise shared wealth through violence. Such greed traps the attackers themselves.

Wisdom is portrayed as a woman calling openly in streets and public places. She offers instruction, but warns those who continually reject it that their own choices will bring calamity. When disaster arrives, neglected counsel cannot simply be recalled at convenience. Those who listen, however, will dwell securely and without fear of evil.

chapters.title: Seek wisdom as hidden treasure

parts.text: A son is urged to receive instruction, treasure commandments, and pursue understanding as diligently as silver or hidden wealth. Such seeking leads to the fear and knowledge of God, because the LORD gives wisdom and protects those who walk uprightly. Wisdom enables a person to understand justice and every good path.

When knowledge enters the heart, discretion guards against corrupt speakers who delight in twisted ways. It also protects from the flattering adulteress who abandons her former companion and covenant. Her path leads toward death. The purpose of instruction is to keep the learner among the upright, whose inheritance endures while the wicked are cut off.

chapters.title: Trust the LORD and practice wisdom toward others

parts.text: The son is told to remember instruction, retain mercy and truth, and trust the LORD wholeheartedly instead of relying on his own understanding. Reverence, turning from evil, honoring God with possessions, and accepting fatherly correction belong together. Wisdom is more valuable than jewels, brings peaceful paths, and is the wisdom by which God founded the earth.

Sound wisdom gives confidence, rest, and protection against fear. The learner must also do good promptly when able, avoid plotting against trusting neighbors, and refuse needless quarrels. Oppressive people are not models to envy. The LORD rejects perversity, blesses the righteous, gives grace to the lowly, and appoints honor to wisdom rather than folly.

chapters.title: Guard the heart and choose the righteous path

parts.text: A father passes on the instruction he received, urging his children to obtain wisdom above all other acquisitions. Loving and embracing wisdom brings preservation, honor, and a worthy crown. He describes instruction as a straight path that allows secure steps and calls the son to hold firmly to it as his life.

The wicked path must be avoided rather than cautiously explored; its travelers become restless until they cause harm. Their darkness contrasts with the growing light of the just. The son is urged to keep wisdom before his eyes and within his heart, guard his inward life, reject crooked speech, and deliberately keep his feet from evil.

chapters.title: Faithfulness within marriage

parts.text: The teacher warns against the seductive speech of the strange woman. Her initial sweetness conceals bitterness, destruction, and a path toward death. The son should stay far from her door rather than surrender honor, years, strength, and wealth to others. Otherwise he may end in public disgrace, regretting the instruction he refused.

The positive alternative is delight in the wife of his youth, pictured as drinking from his own spring. Marital love is to be cherished rather than displaced by another woman’s embrace. All human ways lie before the LORD, and a person’s own iniquities can become binding cords. Refusal of instruction ends in ruin rather than freedom.

chapters.title: Financial snares, laziness, and adultery

parts.text: Someone trapped by a financial pledge is urged to seek release promptly and humbly. The lazy person should learn from the ant’s preparation before poverty overtakes him. The chapter also describes a deceitful troublemaker and lists things the LORD hates, including pride, lies, innocent bloodshed, evil plans, false testimony, and sowing discord.

Parental commands are pictured as a guiding lamp that protects against sexual temptation. Adultery is compared to carrying fire or walking on hot coals: harm cannot be avoided. Unlike theft that may be repaid, betrayal of a marriage brings shame and an injured husband’s jealousy that cannot simply be settled by a payment.

chapters.title: The path of seduction leads to ruin

parts.text: The son is urged to treasure commandments, bind them close, and treat wisdom as a sister. This intimate attachment to instruction will protect him from the flattering words of the strange woman. The command is not merely to recognize good teaching but to keep it inwardly as a safeguard.

The teacher recounts seeing a young man without understanding approach a woman’s corner at twilight. She entices him with kisses, religious talk, a prepared bed, and reassurance that her husband is away. He follows like an animal moving toward slaughter, unaware of the cost to his life. The closing warning says her house has brought down many and leads toward death.

chapters.title: Wisdom calls openly and recalls creation

parts.text: Wisdom calls from public heights, roads, and gates, offering truthful speech and understanding to everyone. Her instruction is worth more than silver, gold, or jewels. She hates pride, evil, and crooked speech, and provides the counsel by which rulers govern rightly. Those who seek and love her find enduring riches and righteousness.

Wisdom describes being with the LORD before earth, mountains, seas, and heavens were established, rejoicing in his work and delighting in humanity. The listeners are therefore called to hear instruction and watch at her gates. Finding wisdom means finding life and the LORD’s favor; rejecting her harms one’s own soul.

chapters.title: Wisdom and folly offer rival invitations

parts.text: Wisdom builds a house, prepares a feast, and invites the inexperienced to leave foolishness and live. The responses to correction reveal character: a scorner resents reproof, while a wise person learns and becomes wiser. The fear of the LORD begins wisdom, and knowledge of the holy brings understanding and a longer, profitable life.

A foolish woman offers a competing invitation from her doorway. She calls the same inexperienced travelers, promising the sweetness of stolen water and secret bread. Her visitors do not recognize that the dead are there and that her guests inhabit the depths of hell. The attractive invitation conceals a fundamentally different destination.

chapters.title: Wise conduct, diligent work, and life-giving speech

parts.text: These proverbs contrast wise and foolish children, honest labor and idle neglect, integrity and crookedness, and righteous speech and concealed violence. Illicit wealth cannot replace righteousness, and failure to gather in season brings shame. Hatred fuels quarrels, while love covers offenses. The wise store knowledge rather than letting reckless words invite destruction.

Instruction, restraint of speech, and truthful lips preserve life and benefit others. The LORD’s blessing brings riches, while folly treats mischief as entertainment. The expectations of righteous and wicked people lead toward different ends: gladness and stability on one side, frustrated hopes and removal on the other. Wisdom’s fruit appears especially in useful and acceptable speech.

chapters.title: Integrity, generosity, and the welfare of the community

parts.text: The LORD rejects dishonest weights and values humility and integrity. Wealth cannot rescue a person in the day of wrath, but righteousness guides and delivers. The conduct of individuals affects the whole city: upright people bring blessing, while wicked speech damages neighbors. Trustworthy discretion, abundant counsel, and caution about guaranteeing another’s debts are commended.

Mercy benefits its giver, but cruelty harms the cruel. Righteousness leads toward life; beauty without discretion is grotesquely misplaced. Generosity can increase what withholding diminishes, and those who refresh others are refreshed. Trust in riches fails, while righteous fruit is pictured as a tree of life. Both righteous and wicked people face recompense.

chapters.title: Instruction, honest work, and truthful words

parts.text: Love of correction is linked with knowledge, while rejecting reproof exposes folly. A good person obtains the LORD’s favor, and righteousness gives a firm root that wickedness cannot supply. The chapter commends a virtuous wife, sound judgment, care for animals, and diligent cultivation rather than empty pursuits. Words and deeds return their fruit to the speaker and worker.

The wise accept counsel, overlook insults, speak truth, and use words to heal rather than wound. Lying lips are hateful to the LORD, whereas faithful dealing pleases him. Prudent restraint contrasts with foolish display; diligence contrasts with idleness. A good word lifts an anxious heart, and the righteous way is described as the path of life.

chapters.title: Correction, companionship, and lasting provision

parts.text: A wise child receives instruction, and careful speech protects life. Diligence satisfies where lazy desire accomplishes nothing. Righteousness guards integrity, pride causes contention, and wealth gathered through labor increases, while wealth obtained through vanity dwindles. Deferred hope makes the heart sick, while fulfilled desire becomes a tree of life.

Respect for instruction provides a life-giving guide, whereas refusing it brings shame. Faithful messengers help those who rely on them, and wise companions shape character for good. The chapter also values an inheritance reaching grandchildren, acknowledges that injustice can destroy the poor person’s produce, and describes loving parental correction. Righteousness and wickedness are again contrasted through their eventual fruit.

chapters.title: Discernment, compassion, and the fear of the LORD

parts.text: Wisdom builds a household, while foolishness tears it down. The proverbs commend truthful testimony, prudent evaluation of one’s path, and caution toward persuasive appearances. A way can seem right yet end in death, and laughter may conceal sorrow. The inexperienced believe everything, but the prudent examine their steps and turn away from evil.

Despising the poor is sinful, while mercy honors their Maker. Productive labor matters more than talk, true witnesses rescue, and the fear of the LORD supplies confidence and a fountain of life. Patience is wiser than quick anger, and a sound heart is better than envy. The chapter connects righteousness with national honor and wise service with a ruler’s favor.

chapters.title: Gentle answers and a teachable heart

parts.text: A gentle answer can turn away anger, while harsh speech provokes it. The LORD sees both good and evil, and his pleasure rests in upright prayer and righteous conduct rather than wicked sacrifices. Wisdom welcomes correction and seeks knowledge. The chapter values a cheerful heart and declares that little with reverence and love is better than wealth or feasting accompanied by trouble and hatred.

Patience quiets disputes, counsel strengthens plans, and a timely word brings joy. The LORD opposes pride, protects the widow, and hears righteous prayer. Greed troubles a household, while careful speech and openness to life-giving reproof mark understanding. Humility comes before honor, and fearing the LORD provides wisdom’s instruction.

chapters.title: Human plans under the LORD’s direction

parts.text: People plan and judge their own conduct, but the LORD weighs motives and directs their steps. Works should be committed to him, pride rejected, and righteousness preferred to dishonest gain. Mercy, truth, and the fear of the LORD turn people from evil. Kings are urged toward just judgment, honest measures, and truthful counsel, since righteousness establishes a throne.

Wisdom is better than wealth, and pride precedes destruction. Humility, prudent speech, and pleasant words sustain life, while gossip divides friends and violence entices others into danger. A seemingly right path may still end in death. Gray hair is honorable when joined to righteousness, and self-control exceeds military conquest. Even the outcome of the lot belongs to the LORD.

chapters.title: Peace, faithful friendship, and restrained speech

parts.text: A quiet home with little is better than abundance joined to strife. The LORD tests hearts, and mocking the poor reproaches their Maker. Love does not keep repeating an offense, while a wise person learns more from reproof than a fool from severe punishment. Returning evil for good invites lasting trouble. Quarrels should be stopped before they overflow like released water.

Condemning the just and acquitting the wicked are equally hateful to the LORD. A true friend loves consistently, and family loyalty is especially evident in adversity. The sayings warn against reckless pledges, corrupt gifts, and foolish children who grieve their parents. Cheerfulness strengthens, bitterness weakens, and even a fool may appear wise when he remains silent.

chapters.title: Speech, careful hearing, and genuine refuge

parts.text: The chapter contrasts a fool’s desire to display himself with the wisdom that resembles a deep, flowing source. Partial judgment, quarrelsome speech, gossip, and laziness bring harm. The LORD’s name is a strong tower for the righteous, unlike the imagined security of wealth. Humility, rather than pride, precedes honor.

A person should hear a matter fully before answering and recognize that an initial account may change when another party is heard. Offended relationships can be harder to repair than fortified cities. Words carry the power of life and death. Finding a wife is called a good gift, and friendship requires faithfulness, with some friends remaining closer than a brother.

chapters.title: Integrity, kindness, and the wisdom to receive counsel

parts.text: Honest poverty is better than corrupt speech. Haste without knowledge misleads, and human foolishness often brings consequences that people wrongly blame on the LORD. Wealth attracts friends while poverty isolates, but false testimony remains punishable. Discretion delays anger and overlooks offenses. Family life can bring grief, yet a prudent wife is a gift from the LORD.

The proverbs condemn idleness and commend obedience, kindness to the poor, and timely discipline. Giving to the poor is described as lending to the LORD. Human plans are many, but God’s counsel stands. Instruction prepares a person for later wisdom, whereas rage, contempt for parents, false witnesses, and mockery lead toward correction and judgment.

chapters.title: Honest dealings and patient judgment

parts.text: Wine can deceive, and avoiding strife is honorable. The lazy person who refuses to plow should not expect a harvest. Integrity blesses children, while claims of personal purity are challenged. The LORD condemns false weights and measures, and even children reveal their character through conduct. Discernment, diligence, and knowledgeable speech are valued above appearance or riches.

Dishonest gain first tastes sweet but ends bitterly. Counsel should guide plans, gossip must be avoided, and parents honored. Instead of avenging wrong, one should wait upon the LORD. Rash vows create snares, and human steps depend upon God. A ruler is preserved by mercy and truth, while both youthful strength and the dignity of age have their place.

chapters.title: Justice is better than impressive sacrifice

parts.text: The LORD directs a king’s heart and weighs motives that people readily justify. Doing justice pleases him more than sacrifice. Diligence is contrasted with haste, honest conduct with deceptive wealth, and a peaceful corner with a quarrelsome home. Those who refuse the poor person’s cry may themselves go unheard. Justice brings joy to the righteous but terror to evildoers.

Pleasure-seeking and idleness consume resources, while wisdom, guarded speech, righteousness, and mercy preserve life. A wicked person’s sacrifice is hateful, especially when offered with malicious intent. False testimony and stubborn pride cannot stand against God’s purpose. No counsel defeats the LORD; even with horses prepared for battle, safety comes from him.

chapters.title: A good name and the words of the wise

parts.text: A good reputation is preferable to wealth, and the LORD is Maker of rich and poor alike. Prudence anticipates danger, humility accompanies reverence, and children need purposeful training and correction. Debt brings dependence, generosity brings blessing, and scoffing fuels contention. Laziness invents excuses, while oppression and attempts to gain favor through wealth lead to loss.

A new appeal introduces words of the wise, intended to be kept inwardly and spoken reliably so trust rests in the LORD. The learner is warned against exploiting the poor, adopting an angry person’s habits, and guaranteeing debts beyond his means. Ancient boundaries must be respected, and skillful diligence is commended as fitting for royal service.

chapters.title: Guard appetite and hold fast to truth

parts.text: The learner is warned to exercise restraint at a ruler’s table, avoid exhausting himself for fleeting riches, and distrust hospitality offered by a grudging host. Boundary theft against the fatherless brings opposition from their mighty redeemer. Instruction and discipline should be welcomed, and parents rejoice when their children’s speech is wise. The fear of the LORD is preferable to envying sinners.

The counsel urges wise companionship, respect for parents, and devotion to truth rather than drunkenness or gluttony. Sexual temptation is a dangerous pit. A vivid description of wine’s effects follows: quarrels, wounds, distorted sight, confused speech, and insensibility to injury. Despite the harm, the drunkard longs to return to drinking, exposing appetite’s enslaving cycle.

chapters.title: Wisdom builds, rescues, and perseveres

parts.text: The learner must not envy destructive people. Wisdom builds a house, strengthens its rooms, and gives better preparation than raw power. Responsibility includes rescuing those being led to death rather than claiming ignorance before the God who knows hearts. Wisdom gives hope, the righteous rise after falls, and another person’s downfall is no occasion for gloating. Reverence for the LORD and king accompanies caution toward rebellion.

Additional sayings reject partial judgment, false testimony, and retaliation. Work should be prepared before a household is built. The teacher then observes an idle person’s overgrown field and broken wall. A little repeated sleep and neglect bring poverty, turning a neglected vineyard into a practical lesson.

chapters.title: Royal wisdom, fitting words, and self-control

parts.text: Proverbs copied by Hezekiah’s men begin with royal judgment: removing corrupt advisers establishes a righteous throne. Humility is better than claiming an honored place and being publicly lowered. Disputes should be handled carefully and privately. Apt words, wise reproof, faithful messengers, and patient persuasion are valuable, while boasts of generosity without delivery resemble clouds that bring no rain.

The remaining comparisons encourage moderation, respect for a neighbor’s space, and sensitivity toward sorrow. False witnesses and unreliable helpers inflict harm. An enemy’s hunger and thirst should be met with food and water, leaving reward to the LORD. Good news refreshes, but moral compromise pollutes. A person without self-control resembles a city with broken walls.

chapters.title: Folly, laziness, and hidden malice

parts.text: Honor is unsuitable for a fool, and careless reliance upon one brings danger. Paired sayings warn both against joining a fool’s foolishness and against leaving him wise in his own eyes. Wisdom requires an answer suited to the danger. Proverbs and responsibility are wasted when placed in foolish hands, and self-conceit leaves even less hope than acknowledged folly.

The lazy person invents threats, turns on his bed, and considers himself wiser than reasoned answers. Meddling in another’s quarrel, deceiving a neighbor as a joke, and spreading gossip all fuel conflict. Pleasant speech may conceal hatred. Hidden malice will be exposed, and schemes such as pits and rolling stones can return upon their makers.

chapters.title: Faithful friendship and diligent provision

parts.text: The chapter warns against boasting about tomorrow and praising oneself. Envy and foolish anger burden others, whereas honest correction from a friend is better than concealed love or an enemy’s kisses. Longstanding friends should not be abandoned. Prudence anticipates danger, and careless pledges or ill-timed behavior can damage relationships. A contentious household is likened to persistent dripping.

People sharpen one another like iron, and faithful service receives its fruit. Hearts reveal character, desire remains difficult to satisfy, and praise tests a person. The closing section urges careful attention to flocks because wealth and political honor do not last automatically. Patient husbandry supplies clothing, food, and support for the household.

chapters.title: Confession, honest labor, and mercy to the poor

parts.text: The righteous possess a courage the guilty lack. Stable government depends upon understanding, while corrupt leadership and oppression ruin the land. Integrity is worth more than riches, and hearing God’s law matters even to the acceptability of prayer. Those who conceal sin do not prosper, but confessing and forsaking it finds mercy. Reverent caution is contrasted with a hardened heart.

Violent rulers, dishonest gain, partial judgment, and haste to become rich bring danger. Diligent labor and faithfulness are commended, and honest rebuke ultimately helps more than flattery. Robbing parents cannot be excused as harmless. Pride provokes conflict, trust in oneself is folly, and generosity toward the poor is blessed. Wicked rule drives people into hiding.

chapters.title: Righteous rule, correction, and freedom from fear

parts.text: Repeatedly rejecting reproof leads to sudden ruin. Righteous authority makes people rejoice, while wicked rulers cause mourning. Justice establishes a land, bribery damages it, and wise people restrain anger that scoffers inflame. The righteous care about the poor person’s cause. A ruler who listens to lies corrupts his servants, while faithful judgment for the poor gives strength to the throne.

Correction benefits children. Where there is no vision, the people perish; keeping God’s law brings happiness. Hasty words, uncontrolled anger, and pride bring consequences, but humility receives honor. Partnership in theft ensnares the participant. Fear of people creates a trap; trust in the LORD brings safety, and true judgment comes from him rather than merely from a ruler’s favor.

chapters.title: Agur’s humility and lessons from creation

parts.text: Agur acknowledges his limited wisdom before the One who governs heaven, wind, waters, and earth. Every word of God is pure and must not be supplemented with false claims. He asks for honesty and sufficient provision, neither poverty that tempts theft nor wealth that encourages denial of God. Further sayings expose slander, dishonor toward parents, self-deception, pride, and exploitation of the poor.

Numbered observations consider insatiable appetites, mysterious paths, social upheaval, small but skillful creatures, and majestic movement. Ants prepare, conies find secure homes, locusts act together, and the spider reaches palaces. The closing counsel urges restraint after foolish self-exaltation or evil planning: provoking anger produces conflict as surely as churning milk produces butter.

chapters.title: A king’s responsibility and a virtuous woman’s worth

parts.text: King Lemuel records his mother’s teaching. He should not squander his strength on women or allow drink to cloud judgment and pervert the rights of the afflicted. Rather than using royal resources for indulgence, he must speak for those unable to defend themselves, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.

The chapter then praises a virtuous woman of surpassing worth. Trusted by her husband, she works skillfully, trades wisely, provides for her household, helps the poor, and speaks with wisdom and kindness. Strength and honor accompany her diligence, and her family praises her. Beauty and charm fade, but a woman who fears the LORD deserves lasting honor for her work.
